comparisons.reason: Both are any-comment binary features over OC_comments with matching null/empty rules, but the construct differs in scope. Left requires a specific, verifiable procedural example: a concrete instance or description of an actual procedure, process, rule, protocol or practice, such as how a legal or institutional process works. Right accepts any particular concrete case, person, organization, event or situation as an example. Right is much broader, because a named person or event that is not a procedure would count there but not on the left. Left also has an explicit rule to ignore quoted OP text, and right does not. The two are a narrower subtype versus a broad construct, so they are not interchangeable.
